prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2017 – Summary (≤500 words)

Overall pitch
- Present the Lib Dems as the strong, pro-European opposition to a likely Conservative majority, ruling out coalition with Conservatives or Corbyn’s Labour.
- Vision: an open, tolerant, united Britain; strong opposition to a hard Brexit.

Brexit and Europe
- Second referendum on the final Brexit deal, with the option to remain in the EU.
- Seek closest possible ties: single market and customs union membership; protect freedom of movement, Erasmus+, EU citizens’ rights, security cooperation (Europol, EAW), research funding, environmental and social protections.
- Safeguard devolved interests and Gibraltar.

NHS and Social Care
- Immediate 1p rise on income tax (and dividends) ringfenced for NHS/social care (~£6bn), moving to a dedicated health and care tax.
- Integrate health and social care; cap care costs; Carer’s Passport and better support.
- Mental health parity: ringfenced funding, strict waiting-time standards, crisis care, end out-of-area placements.
- Workforce: end pay freeze, guarantee EU staff rights, reinstate nurse bursaries, national workforce plan.
- Prevention: public health funding restored; obesity strategy; smoking levy; PrEP on NHS; antimicrobial resistance plan.

Education and Young People
- Nearly £7bn extra for schools/colleges; protect per-pupil funding and Pupil Premium; fair national formula.
- Oppose new grammar schools; restore local role in school places; strengthen SEND support.
- Teachers: lift 1% pay cap; guaranteed CPD; tackle workload; QTS for all.
- Curriculum: slimmed core including PSHE, SRE (consent, LGBT+), arts protected; better careers education.
- Early years: triple Early Years Pupil Premium; more qualified staff.
- Universities: restore maintenance grants; protect openness post‑Brexit; retain research links; quality assurance.
- Lifelong learning/apprenticeships; expand higher vocational routes.

Economy and Taxes
- Eliminate day-to-day deficit by 2020; borrow to invest.
- £100bn infrastructure: 300k homes/year, hyperfast fibre, schools/hospitals, rail (HS2, Crossrail 2), renewables; new Housing & Infrastructure Bank.
- Fair taxes: reverse cuts to corporation/capital gains taxes; tackle avoidance; review business rates; consider land value tax.
- Small business: expand British Business Bank; start-up allowance; scale-up support.
- Work and rights: living wage review; transparency on pay ratios; modernise gig-economy rights; curb zero-hours abuse; scrap tribunal fees.

Environment and Energy
- Five green laws (transport, zero-carbon, nature, buildings, zero-waste).
- Air quality: diesel scrappage; ban new diesel cars/vans by 2025; more ULEZs; clean buses/PHVs.
- Climate/energy: Zero-Carbon Britain Act (net zero by 2050); 60% renewables by 2030; back storage, smart grids, CCS; oppose fracking; cautious on nuclear (no subsidy); stay in Euratom.
- Homes: 4m insulation retrofits by 2022; Band C for all homes by 2035; restore zero‑carbon homes.
- Nature: £2bn flood fund; statutory natural capital targets; expand green/blue spaces; tree planting; stronger animal welfare.
- Zero waste: 70% recycling; food waste collections; 5p coffee cup charge; landfill/incineration reforms.

Families, Housing, Transport, Communities
- Childcare: extend free hours (including for 2-year-olds and 9–24 months for working parents); more paternity leave; flexible work as a day‑one right.
- Fair welfare: uprate benefits; scrap bedroom tax and two‑child limit; reverse ESA/UC cuts; restore young people’s housing benefit; retain pension triple lock (next parliament).
- Housing: 300k homes/year; 10 garden cities; lift council/HA borrowing caps; stronger affordable homes obligations; renter reforms (ban fees, cap deposits, longer tenancies); Rent to Own; tackle homelessness (Housing First).
- Transport: rail investment/electrification; HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2; fix failing franchises; bus powers to councils; 16–21 Bus Discount Card; cycling/walking.
- Rural: universal superfast broadband; protect Post Office/USO; rural services fund.

Rights, Justice, Immigration
- Defend HRA and ECHR; Digital Bill of Rights; roll back bulk surveillance; replace Prevent with community-led approach.
- Equality: tackle pay gaps and board diversity; LGBT+ rights (gender recognition reform, X passports); free period products in schools.
- Policing/justice: +£300m for community policing; body cams; keep EU policing tools; presumption against short sentences; restorative justice; women’s justice board; legal aid/fees review.
- Drugs: decriminalise possession; regulated cannabis for adults.
- Immigration: efficient, fair system; students out of migration stats; post‑study STEM visas; Migration Impact Fund; humane asylum, end indefinite detention; 50k Syrian refugees; reopen Dubs (3k children).

International and Constitution
- Internationalism: 0.7% aid; stronger arms controls (suspend sales to Saudi); NATO 2%; cyber defence; reduced Trident posture (3 boats); human rights promotion.
- Political reform: STV for Commons/local; votes at 16; elected Lords; donation caps; stronger lobbying rules; constitutional convention; federal UK; ‘devolution on demand’ in England; protect devolved settlements and fair funding.
